feedback: Evidence: iteration 1 (69.32, 12 mm, y = 0.05 m, span ±0.03 m, base_speed 1.3, kp 2.5, kd 0.3), reproduced in iterations 4 and 6. Each geometry change away from it lowered the score: the 16 mm footprint (iteration 2, 54.45), y = 0.03 m (iteration 3, 59.64) and the ±0.04 m span (iteration 5, 52.47). Controller changes have also lowered it: base_speed 1.15 (iteration 7, 61.77) and kd 0.4 (iteration 8, 56.44). Line loss has stayed near 1 per run through iterations 0 to 8, so the geometry layout has been mapped and the controller is the lever now. Hold the geometry. Do not change the geometry in response to the next race, because the Integrator's test (kd 0.2) is a controller-only change, and a geometry change would confound it. If the kd 0.2 race returns about 69 with line loss at or below 1 per run, the geometry is confirmed as the platform. Body width does not move the off-track limit, max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) = 0.06 m across your range, so it is not a lever. Expected result for this candidate: no outcome is stated here; the score will reflect the kd change.
requested_changes: Hold the iteration 1 geometry unchanged: five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m, y = 0.05 m, with the wheel, body and mass values as they are.
Do not move the forward offset (y = 0.03 m cost about 10 points in iteration 3) or the footprint (16 mm cost about 15 points in iteration 2) without a controller-based reason.

If the next race shows line_loss_events clearly below 1 per run, you may test one single geometry change later, such as wheel_track, since dynamics levers are untested. If line loss is unchanged, keep the geometry and leave line-loss handling to the Integrator.
